The Panagbenga Festival, also known as the Flower Festival, is an annual celebration held in Baguio City, Philippines. Its history dates back to the 1900s when it was initially conceived as a way to boost the local economy and promote Baguio's flower industry.
The term "Panagbenga" is derived from the Cordillera language, meaning "a season of blooming." The festival was first celebrated in 1996, although flower floats and parades had been organized earlier as part of the city's adaptation to tourism.
Originally, the festival included a week-long series of events featuring flower floats, street dancing, and various cultural performances that showcase the heritage of the Igorot people. Over the years, it has evolved into a month-long celebration every February, attracting visitors from all over the country and abroad.

The Panagbenga Season of Blooming: A Story of Spirits, Sun, and Survival 🌸✨

Reimagined video by: Grand Revel Creatives | Earl Haro

Music arranged by: @cs.musicalproductions (TikTok) | "Dong Dong Ay" by ALAMAT

Panagbenga is more than just a festival; it is the heartbeat of the Cordilleras. Long before the first float moved down Session Road, the indigenous tribes believed these mountains were the Land of the Anito. Every wildflower was seen as a gift from the spirits, and a bountiful bloom was a divine sign of favor for the fertility of the earth.
In those early days, wild sunflowers—associated with the Sun God looking down on the peaks—signaled the start of the dry season, a time for the community to gather in celebration.

But the most powerful "folklore" is Baguio’s own rebirth. Following the devastating 7.7 magnitude earthquake in July 1990, the city stood in ruins. From that despair, a vision of hope emerged. In 1995, Panagbenga was born—a metaphorical "blooming" from the rubble, proving that like a flower breaking through the frost, Baguio could rise again.

Today, the rhythm of the Bendiyan Dance echoes this journey. Once an ancient Ibaloi war dance for victory in battle, it has been reinterpreted into a dance of unity—a celebration of our collective victory over hardship.

From the ancient spirits to the modern streets, we dance, we bloom, and we remember. 🥁🌻🏙️

PANANG CURRY 🥘🌶️🇹🇭

a regional variation of the typical Thai red curry originating from central Thailand and it is also one of my new favorites. 
 
Feel free to substitute the protein with whatever you would like. Shrimp, beef, pork, fish, tofu if your vegetarian. It all works. 

If you have the time on your hands you could make your own curry paste but im using pre made paste to make it easier. 

Ingredients:

1.5 boneless chicken thighs
8oz coconut milk
Palm or block cane sugar to taste
Fish sauce to taste
2tbsp Store bought panang curry paste (mae ploy)
6-7 Kaffir lime leaves
Thai chilis to taste

Optional:
1 red bell pepper

The curry paste does already have salt in it so depending on how much you use you may not need that much fish sauce. Give it a taste before you add anything extra.

Here are quick, must-know facts about the Panagbenga Festival 🌸✨

🌸Panagbenga means “season of blooming” in the Kankanaey language.
🌸It’s held every February in Baguio City, known as the Summer Capital of the Philippines.
🌸The festival started in 1995 as a way to lift spirits and revive tourism after the 1990 Luzon earthquake.
🌸It’s one of the longest-running flower festivals in the Philippines, lasting the whole month.

Highlights include:
🌹Grand Float Parade – massive floats decorated with fresh flowers 🌼
🌹Street Dancing Competition – dancers in colorful, flower-inspired costumes 💃
🌹Flowers commonly featured are roses, chrysanthemums, orchids, and anthuriums, many locally grown in Benguet.
🌹Panagbenga celebrates culture, resilience, creativity, and community pride.

We understand na safety should always be the priority, pero paano naman yung ibang contingents from different provinces who also gave so much effort, time, and sacrifice?
Tiniis namin yung sobrang haba ng parade at yung init ng grass. Sugat-sugat na yung tuhod at paa namin, puro paltos na, and sobrang sakit na ng katawan—but we still chose to continue and finish our performance. Hindi man namin na-perfect yung routine because super init na ng grass and it was already 12:00 PM, we still gave our 101%.

And why did we perform 4th when we were set to be 6th? The program was unorganized, and felt cooked. It was unacceptable and disappointing.

This is not about insecurity or anything. We just want to be enlightened kung ano talaga ang nangyari and how the title was awarded. We’re simply asking for a fair and clear explanation.

Still, thank you Panagbenga 2026. Despite the flaws, we enjoyed and celebrated.

Disappointed but grateful, we remain proud of our performance. ☝🏻✨

The Panagbenga Festival, also known as the Baguio Flower Festival, is a month-long annual celebration held every February in Baguio City, Philippines. The term "Panagbenga" comes from a Kankanaey term meaning "season of blooming" or "a time for flowering."
 
The festival was conceptualized in 1995 to honor Baguio City's flowers and as a way to help the city recover from the devastation of the 1990 Luzon earthquake. It has since become a vibrant display of the rich cultural heritage of the Cordillera region, showcasing various events, exhibitions, and activities that promote the history, traditions, and values of Baguio and the Cordilleras.
